items.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Wynton Marsalis is mentioned only by the [INTERVIEWER] in the context of 1980s music politics; the [INTERVIEWEE] does not mention him or respond to the mention.

ctx.x: I don’t believe much in giveaways in terms of – that happen when people perform and it’s an audience of all kinds of people that are hired as raiders. I think African Game deserved a Grammy, not just two recognitions. It deserved a Grammy, because what got the Grammy was not anywhere near what African Game is. I’m glad I’m giving you the high down and the lowdown. Okay?

I think you’re absolutely right. It’s interesting, because the ’80s kind of started off with a focus on two people in the music, and the music’s much bigger than that. But it was understandable that people were focusing on and excited about the return of Miles Davis, which at the time was a possible return. About a year later, in ’81, he did actually get back into the music game, the business of making music, the art of making music. But the other person who many people feel unfairly received a lot of attention…
I’m not one to go back.
